items.stem: A decision record names a model by family only. A successor cannot tell which model the evaluation measured. The record must name the measured model exactly. Which entry meets the constraint?
options: Attach the full evaluation notebook and every raw response to the record.
Write the exact model ID and the platform in the record.
Record the model family name only, since the family name identifies the model.
Record the API version header as the model ID for the evaluation.
items.rationale: From the 4.6 generation on, a dateless ID names one fixed snapshot. The exact ID and the platform let a successor identify the measured model.
items.trap: A model family name looks like enough, but it does not name the snapshot that the evaluation measured.

items.stem: A decision record names a model ID. The platform posts a retirement notice with a date for that ID. The notice names a replacement model. The team must keep the record accurate and avoid an outage on that date. Which action meets the constraint?
options: Record the retirement date beside the ID, then test the named replacement before that date.
Keep the ID in the record, since a dateless ID is a fixed snapshot that never retires.
Freeze all model work for the year, and rebuild every decision record from scratch.
Add the Usage page CSV to the record as the model version number.
items.rationale: Every model ID has its own retirement schedule, and a notice sets the date. A tested replacement lets the team move traffic before that date.
items.trap: A dateless ID looks permanent, but it is a fixed snapshot that still follows its own retirement schedule.

items.stem: A team writes a decision record for a Claude model in production. A successor must run the system later and must check the decision. Select two entries that meet both needs.
options: Record the model family and let the successor choose the newest model.
Record the workspace spend limit as the model version for the decision.
Record the exact model ID with its platform and deprecation date.
Write the review criteria that reopen the decision as measurable thresholds.
items.rationale: The exact ID, the platform, and the deprecation date tell a successor what runs and when it retires. Measurable review criteria tell the successor when to reopen the decision. (Inference)
items.trap: A model family name looks like a stable reference, but it does not identify the snapshot that was measured.
